common: These facts describe the backend executing tools, not the OS of the chat/desktop client.
Choose every tool, command, executable name and path syntax for its actual target environment.
Prefer portable read_file/list_files/write_file/create_directory/delete_file tools for files and directories; fetch_url for URLs; run_test_suite for tests.
run_command accepts an argv array and never implicitly starts a shell. Shell builtins are not standalone executables.
Use only reported or independently verified executables; PATH availability does not verify versions or installed packages.
MCP, remote and desktop tools may target a different machine; use their reported environment/capabilities.
Environment facts do not grant permissions, remove workspace boundaries, authorize a shell, or permit a host fallback from container mode.
windows: Windows commands require Windows syntax. Do not assume ls/cat/rm/touch/chmod exist. cmd builtins such as mkdir, dir, type and echo require an explicitly authorized shell; prefer portable tools instead.
container: File/directory tools, fetch_url and run_test_suite execute on the backend host; only run_command uses the Linux sandbox. Do not pass host-only executable paths into the container.
posix: Use POSIX paths and commands for Linux/macOS. Do not use Windows drive paths, cmd.exe or Windows PowerShell unless their availability on this target is verified.
unknown_os: OS is not recognized; prefer portable tools and verify command support instead of guessing Windows or POSIX behavior.
